findings.title: Once a keyspace is set, any persistent `USE` failure now makes the pool discard every…
findings.claim: Once a keyspace is set, any persistent `USE` failure now makes the pool discard every new connection, so the pool can never refill. Before this PR such connections were kept with only a warning.

findings.title: The metrics-balancing commit misses one place where an opened connection is dropped: the…
findings.claim: The metrics-balancing commit misses one place where an opened connection is dropped: the excess shard-aware connection branch. `total_connections` still drifts upward there.

findings.title: When the pool worker stops, its active and excess connections are dropped without…
findings.claim: When the pool worker stops, its active and excess connections are dropped without decrementing total_connections.

findings.title: Test keyspace_setup_failure_triggers_refill claims to prove a refill is triggered but…
findings.claim: Test keyspace_setup_failure_triggers_refill claims to prove a refill is triggered but only asserts need_filling() and the flag; it never runs the scheduling loop in run().

findings.title: The unit test fabricates UseKeyspaceError::RequestTimeout for the refill path, which…
findings.claim: The unit test fabricates UseKeyspaceError::RequestTimeout for the refill path, which that path cannot produce because start_setting_keyspace_for_connection has no timeout (its TODO is still present).

findings.title: The two new keyspace tests do not call setup_tracing(), which the repository's…
findings.claim: The two new keyspace tests do not call setup_tracing(), which the repository's contributing guide requires for new tests and which the neighbouring new tests do call.

findings.title: keyspace_setup_failure_preserves_pool_state awaits network operations and…
findings.claim: keyspace_setup_failure_preserves_pool_state awaits network operations and ready_connections.next() with no timeout.

findings.title: Two new tests rebuild PoolRefiller::new inline instead of reusing mock_pool_refiller,…
findings.claim: Two new tests rebuild PoolRefiller::new inline instead of reusing mock_pool_refiller, and three hand-copy the OPTIONS/STARTUP forged-rule fixture from start_simulated_node.

findings.title: The excess-connection accounting rule ('decrement total_connections by len, then clear')…
findings.claim: The excess-connection accounting rule ('decrement total_connections by len, then clear') is hand-copied at three sites instead of being a single clearing helper; in maybe_reshard the decrement (which counts excess_connections.len()) sits 8 lines above the excess_connections.clear() it accounts for.

findings.title: The resharding metrics test never exercises the excess_connections part of the new…
findings.claim: The resharding metrics test never exercises the excess_connections part of the new decrement in maybe_reshard.

findings.title: The commit messages are one-line subjects with no body explaining why
findings.claim: The commit messages are one-line subjects with no body explaining why. The last commit is a fixup for a test added two commits earlier.

findings.title: All four commit messages are a subject line only
findings.claim: All four commit messages are a subject line only. None explains what changed or why, which the contributing rules require.

findings.title: Commit messages are subject-only with no body explaining why, contradicting the checked…
findings.claim: Commit messages are subject-only with no body explaining why, contradicting the checked 'commit messages explain what changes and why' item.

findings.title: All four commit messages are a subject line with no body explaining why
findings.claim: All four commit messages are a subject line with no body explaining why. The PR checklist nonetheless claims 'The commit messages explain what changes and why.'

findings.title: The new public variant ConnectionError::UseKeyspaceError is an addition to the published…
findings.claim: The new public variant ConnectionError::UseKeyspaceError is an addition to the published `scylla` API, but the commit gives no API or changelog note.

findings.title: The keyspace-failure branch repeats the error bookkeeping of the non-shard-aware…
findings.claim: The keyspace-failure branch repeats the error bookkeeping of the non-shard-aware connect-failure branch: it sets had_error_since_last_refill and runs the same `!is_filling() && is_empty()` guard before update_shared_conns.

findings.title: decrement_total_connections calls dec_total_connections once per connection in a loop…
findings.claim: decrement_total_connections calls dec_total_connections once per connection in a loop instead of adding a bulk subtraction to Metrics.

findings.title: Keyspace-setup failure for a newly opened pool connection was downgraded from warn
findings.claim: Keyspace-setup failure for a newly opened pool connection was downgraded from warn! to debug! even though the connection is now discarded rather than kept.

findings.title: The per-connection USE still has no timeout
findings.claim: The per-connection USE still has no timeout. A USE that hangs never yields a keyspace setup error, so the promised refill never happens.

findings.title: The new private enum `ConnectionSetupError` is undocumented and its name collides with…
findings.claim: The new private enum `ConnectionSetupError` is undocumented and its name collides with the public `ConnectionSetupRequestError`/`ConnectionError::ConnectionSetupRequestError`, while it actually classifies pool-admission failures (open vs. USE keyspace) for OpenedConnectionEvent; it also duplicates the new public `ConnectionError::UseKeyspaceError` classification.

findings.title: The forged SET_KEYSPACE RESULT body hardcodes the keyspace name and its length byte,…
findings.claim: The forged SET_KEYSPACE RESULT body hardcodes the keyspace name and its length byte, independently of the VerifiedKeyspaceName set later in the test.

findings.title: The resharding test passes initial_shard_info to start_simulated_node and then…
findings.claim: The resharding test passes initial_shard_info to start_simulated_node and then immediately replaces the rules with ones that advertise no sharding, so that argument has no effect.

findings.title: In full_pool_clears_excess_connections_and_balances_metrics, the timeout result is…
findings.claim: In full_pool_clears_excess_connections_and_balances_metrics, the timeout result is unwrapped with no message, and worker.await afterwards has no timeout. The subject of commit 617139df ('avoid busy-waiting') overstates the change: the test still polls every 1ms.

findings.title: keyspace_setup_failure_preserves_pool_state calls proxy
findings.claim: keyspace_setup_failure_preserves_pool_state calls proxy.finish() before drop(refiller), the reverse of the sibling tests, and so must allow DriverDisconnected. It also skips setup_tracing(), which the neighbouring tokio tests call.

findings.title: The PR's stated validation never ran any metrics assertion or any of the three new…
findings.claim: The PR's stated validation never ran any metrics assertion or any of the three new metrics tests, because they are all gated on the non-default `metrics` feature.

findings.title: Commit de164845 changes metric behavior without any test
findings.claim: Commit de164845 changes metric behavior without any test. Its regression tests arrive only in the next commit, 0d91aa54.

findings.title: The keyspace check now runs before shard-info extraction, the advanced-shard-awareness…
findings.claim: The keyspace check now runs before shard-info extraction, the advanced-shard-awareness mismatch check, maybe_reshard and the shard-aware port update. A new connection's sharder and port are therefore learned only after USE succeeds, and never if USE fails.

findings.title: The PR title and body describe only the keyspace-failure fix
findings.claim: The PR title and body describe only the keyspace-failure fix. They leave out the behavior-changing commit de164845, which changes the total_connections metric on reshard, excess clearing and full-pool clearing.

findings.title: Keyspace setup failures on shard-aware-port connections skip the shard-aware…
findings.claim: Keyspace setup failures on shard-aware-port connections skip the shard-aware fallback/advanced-shard-awareness logic that the Connection error arm applies, and the new arm duplicates had_error/update_shared_conns logic.

findings.title: Metric ownership for a single connection is split: the increment happens in…
findings.claim: Metric ownership for a single connection is split: the increment happens in start_opening_connection's count_in_metrics, but the matching decrement for a keyspace failure happens in handle_ready_connection's Keyspace arm, and every test must copy the increment rule by hand before each synthetic event.

findings.title: New tests copy the OPTIONS/STARTUP proxy rule fixtures from start_simulated_node instead…
findings.claim: New tests copy the OPTIONS/STARTUP proxy rule fixtures from start_simulated_node instead of parameterizing it, and keyspace_setup_failure_preserves_pool_state inlines open_connection+OpenedConnectionEvent three times because the equivalent helper unrequested_connection_event is cfg(feature="metrics")-gated.

findings.title: The doc comment on start_setting_keyspace_for_connection, 'Requires that the event is…
findings.claim: The doc comment on start_setting_keyspace_for_connection, 'Requires that the event is for a successful connection', is stale: the function takes a Connection, not an event, and now produces events that may be failures.

findings.title: Sharder and port learning now has to wait for the per-connection USE, which still has no…
findings.claim: Sharder and port learning now has to wait for the per-connection USE, which still has no timeout. A hung USE delays resharding without limit, and while it is pending `is_filling()` stays true, which suppresses the Broken publication in the new keyspace arm.

findings.title: The new `#[from] UseKeyspaceError` impl on ConnectionError changes which public error…
findings.claim: The new `#[from] UseKeyspaceError` impl on ConnectionError changes which public error family callers see. A broken connection during USE (UseKeyspaceError::RequestError(BrokenConnectionError)) now reaches pool callers as ConnectionError::UseKeyspaceError, not ConnectionError::BrokenConnection.

findings.title: The new variant's description overlaps with its sibling ConnectionSetupRequestError,…
findings.claim: The new variant's description overlaps with its sibling ConnectionSetupRequestError, documented as 'A request required to initialize a connection failed'. A USE sent during connection setup matches that description too.

findings.title: The new Display string 'Failed to set keyspace while initializing a connection: {0}'…
findings.claim: The new Display string 'Failed to set keyspace while initializing a connection: {0}' does not match the wording that every other UseKeyspaceError wrapper uses: "'USE KEYSPACE <>' request failed: {0}".

findings.title: Commit 617139df ('avoid busy-waiting in metrics test') is a fixup of a test introduced…
findings.claim: Commit 617139df ('avoid busy-waiting in metrics test') is a fixup of a test introduced earlier in the same PR (0d91aa54), which replaced yield_now with sleep. It should be squashed into that commit.

findings.title: The keyspace regression fixture matches every QUERY opcode and never verifies that the…
findings.claim: The keyspace regression fixture matches every QUERY opcode and never verifies that the connection sent the expected USE statement.
